groups.note: Municipal, school, and special-district names are keyed from official Natrona November general summaries beginning in 2016 (the earliest official clerk summary in this archive). The Casper mayor is selected by the City Council from its own members at the first regular January meeting and is not on the November ballot; official City of Casper January 2021–2026 regular-meeting minutes name the mayors used here. Official January 2015–2020 mayor-selection minutes were not on the city's public agendas-and-minutes archive at retrieval, so those years remain Not yet collected. The towns of Midwest and Edgerton do not appear on those official November 2016–2026 summaries; current holders are taken from the official Town of Midwest city-officials page and the official Town of Edgerton town-government page, retrieved 2026-11-24. Casper council is filled from official midterm Vote-For-1 and presidential Vote-For-2 results (three members per ward). Official 2014 clerk local results were not available at retrieval, so January 2015–2018 county row offices and the 2014 commissioner class are Not yet collected. The official 2022 general includes a Vote-For-1 commissioner unexpired (Steven Freel). The official 2024 Casper Mountain Fire District Director (unexpired) contest reports only write-in totals and is not filled.

groups.note: Supreme Court justices and the Chancery Court judge are the people in office this January, from official Wyoming Judicial Branch dates and official retention results (shared with other counties). Local rows are 7th Judicial District judges. Where an official Natrona clerk summary prints only a last name, or omits the name (official 2016 Judge1–Judge5 labels; official 2018 DISTRICT COURT JUDGE / CIRCUIT COURT JUDGE), the full name is taken from the official Wyoming Secretary of State Natrona general precinct-by-precinct summary or from the official Wyoming Judicial Branch 7th JD district or circuit page, and that source is cited. Natrona is in the 7th Judicial District; judges of other districts are not copied here. Cynthia K. Sweet’s official appointment is March 2025 (Wyoming Judicial Branch circuit page); January 2025 keeps official 2024 retained circuit judge Brian D. Christensen, and January 2026 lists Sweet.
